subject.title: fix(daemon): prevent gateway OOM crash loops under sustained load

question: On service regeneration, should OpenClaw recompute its own adaptive heap value while preserving only a distinguishable operator override, or intentionally treat every installed heap flag as permanently explicit?
rationale: The implementation cannot distinguish its own previous generated value from a manual override, so compatibility with operator edits conflicts with correct adaptation after host or cgroup resizing; repository policy cannot choose that upgrade contract automatically.

options.title: Track generated versus explicit
options.body: Add durable provenance so regenerated services recompute OpenClaw-generated values but retain genuine operator-selected heap limits, with upgrade and resize tests.

options.title: Always recompute on regeneration
options.body: Replace every installed heap value with the current adaptive calculation and document that manual service-file edits are not preserved.

options.title: Accept first-install-only adaptation
options.body: Keep the current preservation behavior and explicitly accept that later memory changes require operator intervention despite status/doctor diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Track generated versus explicit
recommendation.body: Add durable provenance so regenerated services recompute OpenClaw-generated values but retain genuine operator-selected heap limits, with upgrade and resize tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the adaptive rewrite, adopted the PR, and has the strongest recent history across the affected daemon install and service-environment boundary.
